purpose: Descriptive phenotype-free, predictor-free autosomal coding baseline; not a diagnostic classifier or EPCR estimator.
defined_on: 2026-09-19 before baseline execution; BUB1B already known, not a blinded or preregistered discovery
consequence_tool: bcftools csq 1.24 --local-csq with Ensembl 116 primary-chromosome GFF3
consequence_policy: All supported protein-coding transcripts; variants in a proposed pair must share an affected transcript. No invented haplotypes.

frequency.source: gnomAD exome and genome population allele counts in retained Exomiser 2512 public allele database
frequency.calculation: Maximum AC/AN fraction over available populations with valid positive AN; use counts, not an unset protobuf frequency field
frequency.missing: Separate frequency-unresolved group; absence or AN=0 is not AF=0
frequency.quality_caveat: Database counts do not establish site quality or population callability; investigate candidates separately

pair_policy: Require a shared affected transcript. Keep unknown phase explicitly unknown. Exclude explicit cis pairs from possible-biallelic groups, retaining an audit count. Opposite alleles of a diploid 1/2 call are trans by the source genotype. Unresolved overlapping representations require separate review.
ranking: Descriptive tied tiers: two predicted-disruptive alleles; one predicted-disruptive plus one other protein-altering allele; two other protein-altering alleles. Homozygous genotypes count twice. No gene-size correction, phenotype, disease-gene filter, ClinVar or pathogenicity predictor. Stable gene/allele order only breaks display ties.
limitations: Sequence consequence is not validated loss of function
Transcript relevance and multi-variant haplotypes require follow-up
Not all genes have a recessive disease relationship
Autosomal coding scope excludes sex chromosomes and noncoding, structural, repeat and mosaic explanations
Shared frequency data and known candidate prevent a claim of fully independent clinical confirmation
